`write_DeclareDesign()` generates copy-pasteable DeclareDesign code that reproduces a powerrules calculation through simulation.
The generated code follows Declaration 18.1 in @Blair2023.

## Running the pipeline

Suppose we plan to replicate @Ahler2018, who find that correcting respondents' misperceptions of their out-party reduces affective polarization.
The standard deviation of feeling thermometer responses in the 2020 ANES is 20.8.
We plan to recruit 500 respondents per condition and assume a treatment effect of 3 points (the lower bound of Ahler and Sood's 95% confidence interval).

```{r}
library(powerrules)

result <- from_sd(sd_y = 20.8) |>
  find_power(n = 500, tau = 3)
```

## Generating the DeclareDesign code

`write_DeclareDesign()` takes the result and prints a self-contained DeclareDesign script:

```{r}
write_DeclareDesign(result)
```

## Running the generated code

The generated code runs 500 simulations and reports the simulated power.
Because DeclareDesign uses two-sided tests, the result closely matches the analytical 74% from powerrules for power levels above about 20%.

```{r}
library(DeclareDesign)

my_design <-
  declare_model(
    N = 1000,
    U = rnorm(N),
    potential_outcomes(Y ~ 3 * Z + 20.8 * U)
  ) +
  declare_inquiry(ATE = mean(Y_Z_1 - Y_Z_0)) +
  declare_assignment(Z = complete_ra(N, prob = 0.5)) +
  declare_measurement(Y = reveal_outcomes(Y ~ Z)) +
  declare_estimator(Y ~ Z, inquiry = "ATE")

set.seed(1234)  # so this page shows the same result on every build
diagnosis <- diagnose_design(my_design, sims = 500,
  diagnosands = declare_diagnosands(
    power = mean(p.value <= 0.10)
  ))
print(diagnosis)
```
